notes: Access route: initial direct HTTP GET (plain requests, no impersonation) to the homepage and one nav dump BOTH succeeded (HTTP 200, window.__INITIAL_STATE__.context.country='BE', context.language='nl' -- confirmed genuine Dutch-language Belgian storefront, not a redirect/mirror of FR). robots.txt checked first: no Claude-specific disallow (no ClaudeBot/anthropic-ai/Claude-Web entries); BE/nl sitemap_index.xml is listed there. Rule 3 sanity check: live, real storefront, EUR pricing, standard e-commerce chrome, no closing-down-sale language, DNS resolves to the same Google Cloud LB IP (34.160.107.73) as the FR storefront -- same underlying platform/infrastructure, genuinely separate country/language edition (confirmed independent of S.N. 104 FR: different __INITIAL_STATE__ country/language values, BE-specific URLs and category slugs, and BE's own live Wayback article counts, e.g. Mirrors=318 vs FR's stale 1980 reference, proportional to Belgium's much smaller market -- not a mirrored/duplicate catalogue). HOWEVER: every subsequent request to a /c/ category listing page returned the identical DataDome JS-challenge block seen on FR (403, 781-byte 'Please enable JS and disable any ad blocker' body, same 'dd' cid/hsh cookie pattern) -- including a RE-FETCH of the homepage itself minutes later, which also started 403'ing, confirming (as with FR) that the single initial successful plain-request fetch was a one-time grace window before DataDome's bot-scoring caught up, not a stable route. Ran a full independent Rule 2 sweep on BE/nl specifically (did not assume the FR finding would carry over): 40 curl_cffi impersonation profiles across two passes (chrome99-146 desktop/android, edge99/101, safari15_3-18_0/172_ios/180_ios/184_ios/260_ios, firefox133-147, tor145) -- all 403 identical block; r.jina.ai -- hit Cloudflare's OWN challenge on r.jina.ai's worker (contention, matches brief's known shared-resource behaviour); translate.goog -- reached genuine origin (confirmed via the same DataDome 'dd' challenge script embedded in the translated page, i.e. translate.goog's proxy IP is itself blocklisted by DataDome, not a bypass), later attempt returned HTTP 400; WebFetch -- 403; BE/nl sitemap_index.xml -- 403; the site's own BFF API host (bff-www.maisonsdumonde.com/api, found in window.__INITIAL_STATE__.config.bff.uri, resolves to a different IP 34.149.4.167) -- 403 identically, all 20 curl_cffi profiles also 403 on this host; a session-cookie navigation flow (fetch homepage first with curl_cffi to capture the 'datadome' cookie, wait, reuse session for the category page) -- 403 on both legs. Ran two real-gap cooldown waits (100s, then a further 240s) and retried homepage + category + translate.goog after each -- still 403 both times, showing this is not transient contention but a persistent block, matching the FR precedent exactly. DNS: single IPv4 A-record, no AAAA, no alternate origin to route around (same as FR). Net conclusion: BE/nl is reachable for structure discovery via the one grace-window fetch but DataDome hard-blocks all live count verification identically to FR -- a genuinely independent, freshly-run confirmation that the block is not FR-specific, not a stale finding copied from S.N. 104. Category STRUCTURE below was built from the one successful LIVE nav dump (338 genuine links from the real mega-menu, not invented, not Wayback) cross-checked against S.N. 104's FR structure: most category IDs/hashes are IDENTICAL between FR and BE (e.g. Spiegels/Miroirs=484554f26aa42ef448cafd6fe7ad385e, Vazen/Vases=1e4efd027db117f62efcb2f8c2f61088, Klokken/Horloges=295cfeb7e459cc89149c9cfac915fd68), confirming the same underlying platform taxonomy per company just localized -- this let FR's already-verified 'genuinely decorative despite ambiguous name' findings (e.g. Panelen en letters / Plaques et lettrages; Fotolijsten / Cadre photo) carry over with confidence even though BE's own product titles could not be independently re-checked live. Two known gaps versus FR's 36-row structure: BE's live nav dump did not surface a distinct 'Posters and Prints' node (FR's separate affiches-et-posters) -- only 'Doeken, prenten en andere wanddecoratie' (Canvases, prints and other wall decor) was found, sharing FR's toiles-et-tableaux hash, so it may be a merged BE node or simply not captured by the shallower single-page scrape; and no Lamp Shades (FR's abat-jours) or Jardin-department outdoor-lighting children (Outdoor Floor Lamps/Garden Lamps/Outdoor String Lights) were found in the captured nav -- not fabricated as rows since their presence for BE specifically was not verified. All qty are null and flagged per Rule 1 (no live exact count obtainable); where a Wayback Machine snapshot was independently pulled for BE/nl specifically (structure/reference only per Rule 2, NEVER used as qty) the reference number is quoted in evidence, clearly marked unverified: Mirrors 318 articles (2026-06-08), Vases 134 (2026-06-08), Wall Clocks 66 (2025-09-23), Wall Art/Prints/Wall Decor node 156 (2025-08-12). EXCLUDED as out of scope: Behangpapier (wallpaper, standing exclusion); Kaarsen en theelichtjes (candles/tealights -- could not verify unscented-only split live, default excluded per Home Fragrance rule, same as FR's Bougies); Geurstokjes en geurzakjes (diffuser sticks/scent sachets, home fragrance); LED-lampen (LED lamps -- ambiguous, likely light-bulb replacements rather than fixtures; excluded per the standing light-bulb exclusion since product titles could not be checked live); Deurknoppen en deurdecoratie (door hardware); Decoratieve opberger/Manden/Wasmand/Sieradenhouders/Dozen en kistjes (storage-primary); Bestek (cutlery); Aperitiefschalen en -kommetjes, Wijn- en cocktailaccessoires, Tafelaccessoires, Papieren servetten, Opbergruimte en opslag in de keuken, Bokalen potten en snoepdozen, Opbergaccessoires voor de keuken, Veldflessen en thermosbekers, Brood- en fruitmanden, Dozen voor voedselbewaring, Lunchbox en koeltassen (functional/mixed kitchen tools and storage, excluded for safety, titles not checkable live, mirrors FR's equivalent exclusions); Huisdieren (pets); all of Textiel en tapijten (rugs/curtains/bedding/cushions/table linens, standing textile exclusion); all Tuin/garden department items except outdoor lighting (Tuindecoratie, Buitenpotten en plantenbakken, Tuintapijten, Tuinkussens, Parasols, Lantaarns en kaarsenhouders (garden-specific lantern+candle-holder mixed bucket, excluded as a facet re-cut of the two Home Accessories rows already extracted -- overlap not documented as a separate row since it mixes two product types under one label), Kunstmatige buitenplanten (faux plants), Tuin decoratieve objecten (ambiguous garden decor)); all furniture, bedding, bathroom-fixture, kitchen-appliance and kids-furniture branches. Rule 0 gains: Wandlampen en spotlampen (Wall and Spot Lights, 7beb4879ac8a4669b6cbce8501463f1a) is a genuinely NEW row not present in FR's extracted set -- included per Rule 0.2 (wall lighting branch); Buitenverlichting en decoratieverlichting (Outdoor Lighting, ndf01cf48b9fca173ae2745e481755f51acfa6e0, same hash as FR's luminaire-et-eclairage-exterieur) included per Rule 0.1 rather than dropped as a garden-department item. Rule 0.6: the Kids/'Kids' branch (Kinderdecoratie, Muurdecoratie voor kinderkamers, Kinderspiegels, Verlichting voor kinderkamers, Decoratieve voorwerpen kinderen) exists in the nav but, as with FR, was treated as a demographic facet of the same product types already covered by the main Wall Decor, Mirrors and Lighting rows rather than extracted as a separate branch -- flagged here for the merge step to reconsider, consistent with the FR worker's same call.
